# Baghdad 830 – Institutions, law & governance

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/islamic-830-baghdad.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Written, published law code** [`written_law_code`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_law_code.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. Law is the jurists' reading of Quran and Prophetic precedent, not a code the ruler enacts. Ibn al-Muqaffa' urged al-Mansur (c. 750s) to impose one uniform code; jurists still resist. Al-Shafi'i (d. 820) has just systematised the sources. Local: Yahya ibn Aktham, chief qadi; Ahmad ibn Hanbal; pupils of Abu Yusuf and al-Shaybani (Hanafi school). Elsewhere: Constantinople, the Ecloga (741) and Justinian's Code; Tang China, the Tang Code (653).
- **Rule of law and separation of powers** [`rule_of_law`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rule_of_law.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Everyone agrees God's law stands above the caliph; nobody agrees who interprets it. Al-Ma'mun claims that authority for himself, and the Mihna of 833 is the test. Officials answer to him, not to courts. Local: Ahmad ibn Abi Du'ad (the caliph's party); Ahmad ibn Hanbal (the scholars' party).
- **Independent judges and judicial review** [`independent_judiciary_judicial_review`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/independent_judiciary_judicial_review.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Qadis judge by a law the caliph did not make, but he appoints and dismisses them, and the Mihna will examine every qadi on the createdness of the Quran. Grievances against officials go to the ruler's own mazalim hearings. Local: Yahya ibn Aktham; the caliph's mazalim (grievance) sessions.
- **Habeas corpus and fair trial** [`habeas_corpus_fair_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/habeas_corpus_fair_trial.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Before a qadi the claimant must prove with two upright witnesses and fixed penalties are averted by doubt. The police and the caliph imprison without any qadi, and torture for confession or taxes is routine. Local: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Mus'abi, chief of police; the Matbaq, the caliphs' state prison.
- **Representative government (elected assembly)** [`representative_government`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/representative_government.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Consultation (shura) is praised and means the ruler hearing his chosen counsellors. Allegiance (bay'a) is sworn by notables to a man already designated. No body is elected, and Aristotle's Politics is not translated.
- **Selection of officials by lot (sortition)** [`sortition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sortition.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept low. Drawing lots (qur'a) is lawful for dividing shares or settling equal claims, after Prophetic precedent. Filling an office by lot would look like gambling with God's trust.
- **Direct democracy (citizen assembly voting on laws)** [`citizen_assembly`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/citizen_assembly.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. The Friday mosque is where policy is announced, not decided. Crowds act in riots and in the Baghdad vigilante movement of 817; Athens is a name in Greek books.
- **Secret ballot** [`secret_ballot`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secret_ballot.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Nothing is voted on. Paper and sealed boxes would make it trivial to run, if any body existed that chose by votes.
- **Peaceful transfer of power and loyal opposition** [`peaceful_transfer_of_power`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/peaceful_transfer_of_power.md) — K2, use wrong, make hard, accept low. Harun's succession pact of 802, written and hung in the Kaaba, ended in civil war and al-Amin's death in 813. Al-Ma'mun named the Alid Ali al-Rida heir in 817 (dead 818). In 833 he passes over his son for his brother. Local: Abu Ishaq al-Mu'tasim; al-Abbas ibn al-Ma'mun; Ibrahim ibn al-Mahdi (anti-caliph 817–819, pardoned).
- **Written constitution** [`written_constitution`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/written_constitution.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. The Medina pact is preserved in the Prophet's biography; Harun's Mecca documents were a written settlement of power, and they failed. A charter that binds the caliph himself is unthought. Local: Ibn Sa'd and the biographers of the Prophet in Baghdad.
- **Federalism and subsidiarity** [`federalism_subsidiarity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/federalism_subsidiarity.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. In practice the Tahirids hold Khurasan by inheritance and the Aghlabids rule Ifriqiya for a tribute. Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians run family law and worship under their own heads. Local: Abdallah ibn Tahir, governor of Khurasan; the Catholicos of the Church of the East; the Jewish Exilarch in Baghdad.
- **Treaties, diplomacy and international law** [`international_law_sovereignty`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/international_law_sovereignty.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Al-Shaybani's Siyar (d. 805) sets out war, truce and safe-conduct (aman). Envoys pass to Constantinople and prisoners are exchanged on the Lamos river in Cilicia (805; the next exchange only in 845). Byzantium is an enemy to be bled, not an equal. Elsewhere: Constantinople, Emperor Theophilos (r. 829–842).
- **Secure property rights and land registry** [`property_rights_land_registry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/property_rights_land_registry.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The Sawad has been surveyed for land tax since the conquest and the tax bureau keeps registers. Title rests on witnesses and deeds; fallen officials and their families have everything confiscated (the Barmakids in 803). Local: diwan al-kharaj (land-tax bureau); professional witnesses ('udul) at the qadi's court.
- **Contracts, notaries and merchant courts** [`commercial_law_contract_enforcement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/commercial_law_contract_enforcement.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The Quran orders debts to be written and witnessed; qadis enforce sale, hire, partnership and agency, and formularies for deeds are circulating. Jurists already sell legal devices (hiyal) around the ban on interest. Local: Karkh markets; Hanafi jurists at the qadi's court.
- **Patent law** [`patents`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/patents.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. An inventor's reward is a caliph's gift or a post. Craftsmen guard secrets in the family, and a monopoly would need a caliphal grant.
- **Copyright for authors** [`copyright`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copyright.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Any copyist in the stationers' market may copy any book. The scholarly answer is transmission by audition and licence (ijaza), which protects accuracy, not income. Local: Suq al-Warraqin (stationers' market).
- **Standard weights and measures** [`standard_weights_measures`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_weights_measures.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Coin weights are legal standards (mithqal, dirham); market inspectors test scales, and stamped glass weights are made in Egypt. The ratl and the grain measures differ between Baghdad, Kufa and Basra. Local: the market inspector (sahib al-suq, muhtasib); money changers of Karkh.
- **Census and registration of births and deaths** [`census_vital_registration`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/census_vital_registration.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept low. The army register lists each soldier by name, father and physical description, and tax registers list the dhimmis who owe jizya. Nobody records births, deaths or causes. Local: diwan al-jund (army bureau).
- **Public accounts, audit and budget** [`public_accounts_audit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_accounts_audit.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. A control bureau (diwan al-zimam) checks the other bureaus' accounts; revenue lists by province exist. The usual audit is to arrest a dismissed secretary and squeeze him for what he took. Local: diwan al-zimam; the caliph's secretaries (kuttab).
- **Merit-based civil service (examinations)** [`merit_civil_service`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/merit_civil_service.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Secretaries are trained in Arabic style, accounts and Persian manners, often in secretary families (many of them Persian or Christian); entry is by patronage. No examinations. Elsewhere: Tang China, the civil-service examinations.
- **Universal elementary schooling** [`universal_schooling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_schooling.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Quran schools (kuttab) teach boys to read and write for a fee, and literacy is unusually common among townsmen. Girls are taught at home if at all; nothing is free or compulsory.
- **University (self-governing body of teachers and students)** [`university`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/university.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Teaching happens in study circles in mosques and houses, around one master, with licences to transmit. No chartered body of teachers, no degree; the endowed madrasa is two centuries away.
- **Scientific society or academy** [`scientific_academy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_academy.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The Bayt al-Hikma is the caliph's library and bureau, not an academy. Al-Ma'mun's court comes close, with funded observers, instruments, recorded results (the 'verified' tables) and debates in his majlis. It all depends on one patron. Local: Khizanat al-Hikma (Sahl ibn Harun, Salm); Yahya ibn Abi Mansur, Sanad ibn Ali, Habash al-Hasib; the caliph's majlis.
- **Organised industrial research laboratory** [`industrial_research_lab`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/industrial_research_lab.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. The observation programmes at Shammasiyya (828–829) and Mt Qasiyun (831–833) are a staffed, funded long programme, ending when al-Ma'mun dies. Nothing similar exists for crafts. Local: Shammasiyya observatory, Baghdad; Mt Qasiyun, Damascus (Khalid ibn Abd al-Malik al-Marwarrudhi).
- **Public library and museum** [`public_library_museum`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_library_museum.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The caliph's library is open by favour to scholars and copyists; great men keep private libraries. The real public access is the booksellers' market, where books can be read or copied for a fee. Local: Khizanat al-Hikma; Suq al-Warraqin. Elsewhere: Constantinople, the patriarchal and imperial libraries.
- **Freedom of the press** [`free_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/free_press.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. No press. Books circulate freely unless they touch religion; al-Mahdi hunted 'zindiqs' in the 780s, and from 833 the Mihna makes a doctrine compulsory for officials and scholars.
- **Abolition of slavery** [`abolition_of_slavery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_slavery.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Freeing slaves is a pious act, slaves may buy their freedom by contract, and a concubine who bears her master a child goes free at his death. Al-Ma'mun's own mother was a slave. Abolition is unthinkable. Local: slave market (dar al-raqiq) in Baghdad; Zanj labourers in the Basra salt flats.
- **Women's legal rights and suffrage** [`women_rights_suffrage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/women_rights_suffrage.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. A free woman owns and keeps her property and dower, contracts and can sue; she inherits half a brother's share and is secluded if well-born. Zubayda, Harun's widow, funds wells and cisterns along the pilgrim road until her death (831). Local: Zubayda bint Ja'far; Buran, al-Ma'mun's wife (wedding at Fam al-Silh, 825/826); trained singing slave girls (qiyan).
- **Perpetual endowment (waqf, foundation, trust)** [`charitable_endowment_waqf`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charitable_endowment_waqf.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Pious foundations fund wells, mosques and the poor. Jurists still dispute whether an endowment is irrevocable (Abu Yusuf yes, Abu Hanifa no); the doctrine is being written now. Local: Zubayda's waterworks on the Mecca road.
- **Craft guilds and apprenticeship** [`guilds_apprenticeship`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/guilds_apprenticeship.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Each craft has its own street or market with a headman ('arif) answerable to the inspector. Crafts pass from father to son; whether self-governing guilds exist is disputed by historians.
- **Permanent public health authority** [`public_health_board`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_health_board.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. The market inspector checks bread, meat and weights, and the bimaristan cares for some of the sick. No one counts deaths or orders isolation; epidemics are God's decree. Local: the market inspector; the bimaristan of Harun's reign.
- **Fire brigade, civil police and building rules** [`fire_brigade_police_building_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fire_brigade_police_building_codes.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The shurta polices Baghdad and the gates are shut at night; quarters have watchmen. Markets of reed and wood burn; the inspector polices encroachment on streets. The 'ayyarun gangs of the civil war still rule some alleys. Local: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Mus'abi; Karkh markets.
- **Social insurance and poor relief** [`social_insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_insurance.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Zakat and alms go to the poor, debtors and travellers; registered soldiers draw stipends; the bimaristan treats without fee. Relief is charity or pay, not a fund with contributions.
- **Trade unions and collective bargaining** [`trade_unions_collective_bargaining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trade_unions_collective_bargaining.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Workers have no lawful combination. Troops unpaid do mutiny, and that is the only collective bargaining Baghdad knows.
